To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed an inert gas condensation method for the production of iron nanoparticles, and have demonstrated that these nanoparticles are suitable for use in magnetic recording media.

1) the inert gas condensation method can be used to produce nanometer-sized Fe and Fe-oxide particles; 2) the surface passivation layer thickness can be controlled to a certain degree; 3) the coercivity and magnetization of the samples are similar; and 4) the hysteresis loops are different.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a simple and inexpensive method of synthesizing Fe nanoparticles.
the preparation of Fe and Fe-oxide nanoparticles and the characterization of these materials by x-ray diffraction, transmission electron microscopy, and magnetic hysteresis measurements.
the development of a novel method to produce nanoparticles of iron and iron oxides, the characterization of the resulting particles and the measurement of their magnetic properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Fe nanoparticles produced via inert gas condensation are single domain and exhibit a single domain hysteresis.
the Fe/Fe oxide samples are single domain and the Fe/oil immersed samples are multidomain.

the surface passivation technique is more effective in preventing complete oxidation of the Fe particles than the oil immersion technique and that the Fe/FeO samples are more suitable than the Fe/oil for magnetic recording applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Fe-oxide passivated samples were single domain while the oil immersed samples were a mixture of single domain and multi-domain particles.
the Fe/Fe oxide samples were single domain particles, whereas the Fe/oil sample consisted of a mixture of single domain and multidomain particles.
the Fe-Fe oxide samples exhibited a higher volume fraction of Fe oxide and a lower volume fraction of Fe than the Fe/oil sample.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the inert gas condensation method is an effective means of producing nanoparticles of metallic iron.
the Fe-oxide passivation layer on the Fe nanoparticles was sufficiently thin that the nanoparticles were able to exhibit a single component hsteresis loop.
the Fe-oxide passivation layer on Fe nanoparticles can be used to protect the Fe core against oxidation.
